newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firm as market stays tight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firm as market stays tight.

text.p: Interbank rates firmed across the board on Tuesday as market liquidity remained tight, dealers said.
They said the tightness was caused by a mismatch of funds, held mostly by foreign banks.
"The market is still tight as money is not spread among market players. The foreign banks are long while local banks are short," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
"The tightness was initially in the short-end but long-term rates are also rising now," he said.
One- and two-week money were at 8.0/8.50 percent against 7.70/80 on Monday.
The one-month rate was at 8.0/8.20 percent from 7.60/90 while three-month money was at 8.0/8.10 percent against 7.50/80.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to stay above eight percent, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 8.0 and 8.5 percent on Monday.
Dealers said liquidity was unlikely to improve this week and rates were expected to stay firm.
A 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Tuesday will be matched by a maturity of an issue of a similar amount on Friday, they said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange extended losses in thin early trading, futures dealers said.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down five points to 92.37, or an implied yield of 7.63 percent.
September contract fell four to 92.51, or 7.49 percent while December was down one to 92.58, or 7.42 percent.
